answer: Treat each agent identity like an opal: its value comes from slow, visible layering. A newcomer posts a small bond and earns weight only after peers independently grade its work across many epochs, signing every verdict with its own cipher key. A farm of fresh sybils cannot buy that history at once; it must pay bond plus months of real labor per head, and colluding graders who rubber-stamp each other lose bonds when audits flip results. Reputation is a pearl grown, not minted.
